name: MarginaliaColumns
description: A column of text with a narrow margin beside it, each note held level with the paragraph it belongs to

--marg-measure.description: The text column. Its own measure, independent of the note column, because the two are different kinds of reading and want different line lengths.

--marg-note.description: The note column, as a fixed width rather than a fraction. Give it a fraction and notes get wider as the window does, which is backwards: a note is a short aside and wants a short line.

--marg-gutter.description: Between the text and its notes. Wide enough that a note reads as marginal rather than as a second column of equal standing.

--marg-step.description: The vertical gap between blocks. It is also what the level modifier cancels, so changing it keeps a levelled note aligned.

--marg-rule.description: The rule down the margin, used by the ruled modifier and by the narrow layout where the note sits under its paragraph.

notes: A note is a grid item in the same row as its paragraph, and that is the whole trick. Float it and it sits wherever the text happened to reach; position it absolutely and it holds still while the paragraph reflows to a different height, so the note explaining the third sentence ends up beside the fifth. As a grid row the pair cannot come apart, at any width, with no measurement and no script
The note column is a fixed measure rather than a fraction. Two independent widths, not one width split two ways: the text keeps its measure and the note keeps its own short line

The note aligns to the top of its row. Stretched or centred, a two-line note beside a nine-line paragraph sits halfway down and stops looking like an annotation of the first sentence, which is what it is
The note must follow the element it annotates in the source. That is what makes it read correctly to a screen reader and what lets the narrow layout put it directly underneath
Below 54rem it becomes one column with the note indented and ruled under its paragraph, so it still reads as an aside rather than as the next paragraph
